prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a finished, extremely polished desktop WEB APP interface for BirdRadar, landscape 1536x1024. Edge-to-edge actual screen design, no computer device, no perspective frame, no marketing poster. First reference image is MATERIAL ONLY: luminous translucent milky silicone / latex film, cyan, lilac, ice blue, pale rose, thin gold fringes, silky microscopic line detail and transparent overlapping layers. Translate it into GEOGRAPHIC migration-density fields conforming to a real map, never a floating abstract sculpture. Second reference is existing bird stamp ART DIRECTION: perforated cream paper edge, dark botanical stamp, a bird as focal artwork. Upgrade stamp printing with prismatic Balatro-inspired holographic foil, embossed metallic outlines, tasteful diffraction and angle highlights; maintain bird identity and crisp typography. UI chrome is quiet matte midnight blue; reserve iridescence for the geographic heat field and stamps. Readable clean humanist sans typography, editorial serif for bird names, precise generous spacing. No neon cyberpunk, no generic dashboard card grid, no big metrics, no made-up live data. Keep coastline, relief and fine country/city labels readable THROUGH heat layers. The route core is denser/milkier, periphery semitransparent, overlapping ribbons form pale luminous interference. Some tiny flowing particles follow the corridor. Distinguish colours using a small legend. This is a conceptual visualization, not a scientific plot: include a clearly readable bottom note exactly "Concept preview · illustrative heat field". Real data provenance text can say "Historical tracking · Movebank". Main navigation: "BirdRadar" then "Explore", "Stamps", "Lights Out", "About". Every image must show a complete usable composition with species selector, map controls, timeline and stamp content. No watermark. COMPOSITION A — Immersive weather atlas. A slim 72px top navigation, then a full-bleed dark terrain map filling the rest of the screen. Show Europe and Africa geographically correct, Atlantic to left, Mediterranean clear, map occupying 85% of the attention. A beautiful BROAD, soft continuous layered heat corridor flows from Germany through France and Spain down northwest Africa into Senegal, 2-3 translucent branching fields in ice cyan, lilac, and soft peach, draped closely on geography, deep luminous milky core with hairline contour filaments. This is the hero, not a thin glowing airline arc. Top left over map is elegant title "The sky is always moving." about 38px with small supporting text "Explore the journeys that connect our world." Below title one narrow species selector "White stork" and pill "Historical". On right float an understated 300px matte translucent collection drawer with heading "Field collection", one medium large portrait foil postage stamp of a WHITE STORK in flight, visually printed on dark stock with silver iridescent perforations and thin prism coating, titled "WHITE STORK"; a second small stamp peeks from behind. Caption "Ciconia ciconia" and button "Explore species". Place a tidy translucent timeline bar along bottom of map, January to December, September selected, play icon, text "Seasonal journeys". Lower left small legend "Tracked-sample density" Low to High using the same translucent colour material. Design feels like Apple Weather at midnight crossed with a carefully curated natural history collection. Complete crisp interface; layered membrane fills geography rather than filling black empty space.
